about.covenant.p1: Yours forever: no account, no ads, no tracking, nothing sent anywhere. Your library — notes, tags, threads — is saved as ordinary files on your device that you can back up or move. The app is free.
about.covenant.title: THE COVENANT
about.heading: About Plumbline
about.lede: A Bible-study tool: a parallel-passage reader with an optional Full-study tier of Strong's, morphology, cross-references, and corpus analytics. Everything runs locally and offline.
about.provenance.p1: KJV text via eBible.org; Strong's via Open Scriptures (CC-BY-SA); morphology from OSHB (CC-BY 4.0) and Robinson's public-domain Textus Receptus tagging; cross-references from the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge via openbible.info. Full credits are in BIBLIOGRAPHY.md.
about.provenance.title: PROVENANCE
about.sideload: Sideloaded builds do not update automatically.
about.text.p1: The Holy Bible — the traditional English text, in the public domain.
about.text.p2: The text is the KJV, always. An optional modernization marks where the American King James Version (1999, public domain) words a verse differently — a dotted underline; tap one to see the KJV word it replaced. It is a reading aid over the same text, not a second translation and not a simplified one: what you memorize, present, copy and share is the KJV whether it is on or off.
about.text.title: THE TEXT

guide.church.p1: Settings ▸ Church holds your congregation's name, a line about it, and a link. It travels in the links and QR codes you share, and nowhere else — no account, and nothing is sent anywhere.
guide.church.p2: It matters because a stranger who reads the gospel on their phone still needs somebody to sit next to on Sunday. Fill it in and every Bible you hand out says where to find you.
guide.church.title: Set your church
guide.gospel.p1: Present is the mode for handing your phone to somebody, or putting the text on a screen: fullscreen, high contrast, one passage at a time, no chrome to explain. It opens on the Romans Road, ready to walk through.
guide.gospel.title: SHARE THE GOSPEL
guide.lede: Whatever you came here to do, start with the thing you want — the rest of the app arranges itself around it.
guide.map.p1: The book and chapter grids in Go to… are tinted by how you have read: gold for a chapter you have never been through, copper while you are partway, sage once you have read it through. A book takes the blend of its chapters, weighted by length, so its chapters always add up to it.
guide.map.p2: On top of the colour, a chapter glows the longer it has been since you read it — nothing for the first month, building to a full glow at a year. That is the whole point of the map: it shows you where you have not been lately. It is not a score, and nobody sees it but you.
guide.map.p3: Reading is counted generously. A chapter fills as you move through it at a natural pace — flipping past credits nothing, and neither does leaving it open — and it counts as read through at 90%, so there is never a last verse to chase.
guide.map.p4: If you read a chapter in a paper Bible, press and hold it in Go to… (or right-click) to mark it read, or use Mark whole book read at the top — pick the date it was read.
guide.map.title: Keeping track of where you have read
guide.memorize.p1: Any verse (or a passage, as one chunk) can become a memorization card. The drills are first-letter prompts, progressive blank-out, and typed recall; the schedule is the proven spaced-repetition algorithm, so review comes back exactly when you are about to forget.
guide.memorize.p2: The memorize hub shows what is due, a map of the canon shaded by what you know, and a heatmap of the days you turned up.
guide.memorize.title: HIDE IT IN YOUR HEART
guide.plain.p1: Choose “Modernized” under Wording in Settings. It marks the words the American King James Version puts differently — tap one to see what it replaced. The text stays the King James: nothing you memorize, present, copy or share is changed by it.
guide.plain.title: If the older English is hard going
guide.preach.p1: Open the thread in Present and it becomes your outline: the passages advance one at a time, big enough to read from across a room, in the order you set. The same thread you built studying is the one you teach from and the one you hand out afterwards.
guide.preach.title: Then preach it
guide.read.p1: One to three panes sit side by side; the ＋ / ✕ in the pane strip add and remove them. Each pane has its own book and chapter and scrolls on its own, so you can hold two passages open together.
guide.read.p2: Go to… walks Testament, then book, then chapter — every step a big target. Left / Right (or [ / ]) step chapters and roll across book boundaries; Alt+Left / Alt+Right walk back and forth through where you have been.
guide.read.p3: Hold Shift while scrolling to move every pane together, which is how you read two accounts side by side without losing your place in either.
guide.read.title: READ THE BIBLE
guide.shareThread.p1: Any thread can be handed over as a link or a QR code — from Present, or from the thread itself. Whoever opens it lands in the first passage with the whole trail in front of them, in their own copy of the app, offline from then on.
guide.shareThread.p2: This is the way to leave someone with something after a conversation: they keep the passages you walked through, in order, instead of a photo of a page.
guide.shareThread.title: Share a thread with someone
guide.study.p1: Ctrl+click (or double-click) a word for what is underneath it: its Strong's entry, every way the King James renders that same word elsewhere, cross-references, and — with the analysis tiers on — morphology, same-root words and the concept map.
guide.study.p2: Search takes a word, a phrase, or a reference. A reference (John 3:16, 1 Cor 13, psalms) jumps there; a word or phrase lists ranked hits, and every hit in the chapter you are reading is banded as you go. A bare Strong's code (H430, G26) lists every verse tagged with it.
guide.study.title: STUDY A PASSAGE
guide.tags.p1: Tags are labelled sets of verses and concepts — the slow way a topic accumulates as you keep running into it. Tag a verse whenever you run into the idea again, and the tag becomes the list you wished you had kept.
guide.tags.title: Collect a topic over time
guide.teach.p1: A thread is a trail you make: passages in your order, for your reason. It is the tool for a sermon, a lesson, a Bible study, or an argument you want to be able to walk someone through twice.
guide.teach.p2: Right-click (or long-press) a verse and choose Add to thread… — pick a thread you have already started, or name a new one. Each entry keeps the words you selected and takes a note of its own, and the thread itself has a running notes document for the shape of the whole thing.
guide.teach.title: PREPARE TO TEACH
guide.title: Using Plumbline
guide.weaves.p1: A weave is a connection you FIND — the same event in three Gospels, a prophecy and its fulfilment, an Old Testament verse and the New that quotes it. Point two panes at linked passages and the connector lines draw themselves; no mode to enter.
guide.weaves.p2: That is the difference from a thread. A weave is in the text whether or not you noticed it, and you will stumble back into it for years. A thread is yours, and it is in the order you chose. If the connection is in the text, weave it; if the connection is your point, thread it.
guide.weaves.p3: The Map and Constellation views show the whole weave library at once. Weaves that shipped with the app began as AI-generated study aids and say so — approving one, from its compare card, is how it graduates to something you have checked against the text yourself.
guide.weaves.title: Follow what the text says about itself
guide.yours.p1: Right-click a verse to copy it, copy the chapter, tag it, add it to a thread, or write a note in your own words. Your notes get a gutter mark and a “your note” line in the study panel.
guide.yours.p2: The theme button cycles light, a candlelight-warm dark, a true-black night, and the system theme. Your theme, text size, margins and last reading position are all remembered.
guide.yours.p3: Everything you write is yours and stays on your device. Settings ▸ Back up (.zip) exports all of it — notes, tags, threads, weaves, memory work and your reading history — and the same archive restores on a phone or in a browser.
guide.yours.title: MAKE IT YOURS

intro.beforeShareSub: You can share the gospel with someone from this app. If they keep the app afterwards, this is how they find your church.
intro.churchWhy: If you add your church, the links and QR codes you share contain your church information, so whoever you hand the Bible to can also find your church. It stays on your device and your data remains private.
intro.curious.p1: For thousands of years this text has been the foundation of civilizations and of the lives of individuals. People have been killed for reading it and for sharing it.
intro.curious.p2: It contains the history of our world from its creation to the incarnation of its Creator here on earth with us. He came to save us because he loves us:
intro.curious.p3: Whether you are just curious or returning to faith after a long time, there is treasure here for you:
intro.curious.p4: If you are having trouble believing, you're not alone — someone said exactly that to Jesus himself:
intro.curious.p5: I encourage you to read this book starting with the book of John, and to pray that if God is real, he would reveal himself to you. I've known many people for whom that prayer has been answered:
intro.curious.struggle: If you are in a difficult place in your life, ask God to help you with your struggles:
intro.curious.title: I'm glad you're curious about the Bible.
intro.humanDesc: Curated scholarship: how the text renders each original word (agapaō → “love” ×27 · “beloved” ×13…), word grammar, the same root traced across the testaments, and the Treasury's cross-references.
intro.humanShort: Curated scholarship: how the text renders each original word, word grammar, the same root traced across the testaments, and the Treasury's cross-references.
intro.machineDesc: Statistical patterns: the words a word keeps company with, and where in the Bible it clusters.
intro.machineShort: Statistical patterns: the words a word keeps company with, where in the Bible it is most used, and where its repetitions cluster.
intro.pathCuriousDesc: I'm not sure what I believe — where do I start?
intro.pathEstablishedDesc: Set up your Bible for study and memorization and prepare to share the good news with others.
intro.pathNewDesc: Where to start if you have just put your faith in Jesus.
intro.pathSharingDesc: Share the gospel and your church from your phone.
intro.provenance: Every piece of evidence is marked with where it comes from — ✝ the text · † scholarship · ≈ machine.
intro.sub: The Holy Bible in a free, offline app. Where would you like to begin?
intro.subShort:
The Holy Bible, free and offline.
Where would you like to begin?
intro.tapHint: Tap any verse reference to open it.
intro.tiersSub: Reading, search, memorization, tags, and notes are all available in this application. Choose which additional analysis tools are installed with the Bible.
intro.title: Welcome to Plumbline
intro.welcome.blessing: May the peace and joy of Christ be with you, and may you share that peace and joy with others. God bless you!
intro.welcome.church: Being part of a local church is a great way to grow in your faith and connect with believers.
intro.welcome.churchMerged: Being part of a local church is a great way to grow in your faith and connect with believers. If someone shared this app with you, consider reaching out to them or attending a Sunday morning service at their church.
intro.welcome.churchNone: If someone shared this app with you, consider reaching out to them or attending a Sunday morning service at their church.
intro.welcome.churchShared: This Bible was shared with you by {church}. Start there: they would be glad to see you, and whoever gave you this can introduce you.
intro.welcome.devotional: A 30-day devotional has been started for you. Each day gives you a passage to read, a short reflection on it, and one thing to do. It appears on the reading screen each day, and you can find it any time under Study.
intro.welcome.forgiven: One day you will be perfected, but not yet, and so while you are here, you are imperfect but you are forgiven:
intro.welcome.kept: No one can take it away from you, and you can know that for certain:
intro.welcome.lead: There are some next steps you can take to grow in faith:
intro.welcome.loved: Know that Jesus loves you, and if you trust in him for your salvation, then you have eternal life:
intro.welcome.memorize: This app can also help you memorize scripture — hiding the word in your heart is a wise and helpful thing to do.
intro.welcome.read: The next page will open in the book of John, which is a great place to start reading the inspired, inerrant word of God. You've been linked the King James Version, which is the closest to the original texts and has been used for hundreds of years by millions of believers. If you have trouble with the older English, turn on the Plain-English overlay in Settings: it marks the words the American King James Version puts differently, so a modern wording is a tap away without ever leaving the King James text.
intro.welcome.struggle: If you are in a difficult place in your life, ask God to help you with your struggles:
intro.welcome.title: I'm so glad you've put your faith in Jesus!
intro.welcome.wisdom: I highly recommend you read your Bible as it is rich with wisdom on how to navigate this world and how to serve our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ:
intro.wordingLater: You can change this any time in Settings.
